title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: our monolithic .github/workflows/ci.yml has grown slow and fragile. This PR splits the single workflow into focused pipelines (lint, unit/integration tests, release automation) and extracts shared pieces into reusable workflow templates. Primary goals: 1) reduce average CI latency by enabling faster, cache-friendly runs for lint and unit tests; 2) improve cache hit-rates and concurrency behavior by changing cache key composition and allowing parallel cache restore/save where safe; 3) bump GH Actions and key third-party actions to pinned stable revisions; 4) simplify release automation so dry-runs and publish steps are logically separated and easier to audit. What changed (high level): created .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml; added .github/workflow-templates/ci-shared.yml to centralize matrix generation, envs, and common steps; introduced cache helper action to compute deterministic keys; updated package.json devDependencies used by CI (eslint, jest) and synchronized node-version across workflows. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and verify triggers - [x] Consolidate common template - [x] Update cache keys and parallelism strategy - [x] Pin GH actions to specific SHAs - [x] Run full CI and release dry-run - [x] Update docs/ci.md with workflow overview Notes: initial run exposed a node-version mismatch in a few runners which caused snapshot test failures; fixed by aligning tool-versions in the shared template. CI was flaky on the first attempt due to cache key collision under high concurrency; adjusted key to include matrix.hash and workflow run id for save to avoid evictions. This PR is intended to be non-breaking for contributors; it only affects how CI runs and the release automation flow (no change to runtime code paths).

review_comments: Adrian Patel: Nice decomposition. Question: can we avoid duplicating matrix definitions? Suggest moving matrix shape into template and letting each workflow import it via inputs.
Maya Chen (author): Implemented — moved matrix to ci-shared.yml and added inputs for job-specific filters. Updated test.yml to pass filter input for integration jobs.
Lina Gomez: Cache key change looks promising but can we guarantee deterministic keys across runners? Please ensure node_modules cache includes package-lock hash.
Maya Chen: Added package-lock.json hash to restore key and included matrix.hash for job-level uniqueness. See scripts/ci/cache-key.js for details.
Samir Reddy: Release job needs additional guard. Add explicit manual approval for publish to npm and require successful e2e in dedicated run before publish.
Maya Chen: Added concurrency/approval gate for publish job and separate dry-run job that runs on tags only. Updated release.yml accordingly.
Adrian Patel (approval): LGTM after fixes. Also verified workflows run shorter on sample runs.
Lina Gomez (approval): Approved. Observed ~28% median runtime reduction for lint+unit runs on matrix samples.
release_notes: Split CI into three focused workflows (lint, test, release) to improve developer feedback loop.
Improved cache key strategy and allowed safe cache parallelism to reduce CI latency and evictions.
Pinned and bumped GH Actions and a few dev-dependencies used by CI (eslint, jest).
Separated release dry-run from publish and added manual approval gate for publishes.
summary: Refactors CI by splitting workflows, centralizing shared templates, improving cache keys/parallelism, and hardening release automation. Measurable improvement in CI latency and cache hit rates.
notes_for_ops: No runtime code changes. Ops: update internal CI runners to ensure node version alignment if you maintain custom runner images; review new release approval policy.
